translations.text: The beginning of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: "Behold, I will send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your ways before you."
"The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the ways of the Lord and make his paths straight."
John was in the wilderness, baptizing and preaching the baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
And all the region of Judea and all the people of Jerusalem went out to him, and they were all baptized by him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.
And John was clothed in a garment of camel's hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.
He preached and said: "Behold, one mightier than I is coming after me, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.
I baptize you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."
And it came to pass in those days that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
And immediately, as he came up out of the water, he saw the heavens opened and the Spirit of God descending upon him like a dove.
And a voice came from heaven: "You are my beloved Son; in you I am well pleased."
And immediately the Spirit led him out into the wilderness.
And he was there forty days, being tempted by the devil, and he was with the wild beasts, and the angels ministered to him.
And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the Gospel of the kingdom of God,
and saying: "The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near; repent and believe in the Gospel."
And as he was passing by the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting nets into the sea, for they were fishermen.
And Jesus said to them: "Come, follow me, and I will make you fishers of men."
And immediately they left their nets and followed him.
And going on a little farther, he saw James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, and they were mending the nets in the boat.
And he called them. And immediately they left Zebedee their father in the boat with his hired workers and followed him.
And they went into Capernaum. And immediately on the Sabbath day he entered their synagogue and taught them.
And the people were astonished at his teaching, for he taught them as one who has authority, and not as their scribes.
And there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out
and said: "Ah, what have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? You have come to destroy us. We know who you are, the Holy One of God."
Jesus rebuked him and said: "Be silent, and come out of him!"
And the unclean spirit threw him down, and cried out with a loud voice, and went out of him.
And all were amazed, so much that they questioned one another and said: "What is this new teaching? For with authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him."
And the report about him went out through all the region of Galilee.
And he went out from the synagogue and came to the house of Simon and Andrew, with John and James.
Now Simon's mother-in-law lay sick with a fever. And they told Jesus about her.
And he came and took her by the hand and raised her up; and the fever left her, and she got up and served them.
And when evening came and the sun was setting, they brought to him all the sick and those possessed by demons.
And the whole city was gathered before the door.
And he healed all of them of evil diseases and of various kinds of sicknesses, and he cast out many demons; and he did not allow the demons to speak, for they knew him, that he was the Christ.
And at daybreak, very early while it was barely dawn, he got up and went out from there, and went away to a desert place, and there he prayed.
And Simon and those who were with him followed after him.
And they found him and said to him: "Everyone is looking for you."
But Jesus said to them: "Come, let us go to the nearby villages and towns, so that we may preach there, for this is why I was sent."
And he preached in their synagogues and throughout all Galilee, and cast out demons.
Then a leper came to him, pleading with him; and he knelt down and said to him: "Lord, if you will, you are able to make me clean."
And Jesus had pity on him, and stretched out his hand and touched him and said to him: "I will; be clean!"
And as soon as he said this, the leprosy immediately left him, and he was made clean.
And he spoke sternly to him and immediately sent him away.
And he said to him: "See that you tell no one, but go and show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."

But he went out from there and began to proclaim it widely and to spread the word around, so that he could no longer openly enter a city, but stayed outside in desert places. And people came to him from every side.
And after a few days he went again into Capernaum; and it was heard that he was in the house.
And immediately a great crowd of people gathered there, so that there was no longer room even in front of the door; and he spoke the word to them.
And they came to him bringing a paralyzed man, carried aloft by four men.
And when they could not get near him because of the crowd, they stripped off the roof of the house where he was, and removed it, and let down the bed on which the paralyzed man lay.
And Jesus saw their faith and said to the paralyzed man: "Child, your sins are forgiven you!"
Now some of the scribes were sitting there, and they were reasoning in their hearts and saying,
"This man is speaking blasphemy. Who has the power to forgive sins but God alone?"
And Jesus at once perceived in his spirit that they were reasoning this way in their hearts, and he said to them, "Why are you reasoning about these things in your hearts?
Which is easier: to say to this paralysed man, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Rise, take up your bed and walk'?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins" — he said to the paralysed man,
"I say to you: rise, take up your bed and go to your house!"
And at once he rose, took up his bed and went out in front of everyone, so that they were all amazed and glorified God, saying, "We have never seen anything like this."
And he went out again to the seashore, and all the people were coming to him, and he was teaching them there.
And as he was passing by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him, "Follow me!" And he rose and followed him.
And it happened that as he was reclining at table in his house, many tax collectors and sinners were sitting with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many there, and they were following him.
And when the scribes and the Pharisees saw that he was eating with tax collectors and sinners, they said to his disciples, "Why does he eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
And Jesus heard this and said to them, "Those who are healthy do not need a physician, but those who are sick. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance."
And the disciples of John and of the Pharisees were fasting, and they came to him and said to him, "Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?"
Jesus said to them, "The sons of the bridegroom cannot fast while the bridegroom is with them.
But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken up from them, and then they will fast, on that day.
No one puts a new patch on an old garment; otherwise the new patch tears away from it the sound part of the old as well, and a worse tear is made.
And no one pours new wine into old wineskins, so that the new wine may not burst the skins, and the wine be spilled and the skins be ruined; rather, new wine is poured into new wineskins."
And it happened that he was passing through the grainfields on the sabbath, and as they went along the way his disciples began to pluck the heads of grain.
And the Pharisees said to him, "Look, what are your disciples doing on the sabbath that is not lawful to do!"
And Jesus said to them, "Have you never read what David did when he was in need and he and those with him were hungry?

How he entered the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the bread of the offering, and gave it also to those who were with him, which it is not lawful to eat except for the priests alone."
And he said to them, "The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath.
Therefore the Son of Man is lord even of the sabbath."
And again he entered the synagogue. And there was a man there whose hand was withered.
And they were watching him to see whether he would heal him on the sabbath, so that they might accuse him.
And at that time Jesus said to the man whose hand was withered: "Get up and come forward into the middle!"
And Jesus said to them: "Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil? To save a life or to kill?" But they were silent.

And he looked around at them with anger, grieved at the blindness of their hearts, and said to the man: "Stretch out your hand!" And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored again, like the other one.
And when the Pharisees went out from there with the Herodians, they plotted against him, how they might destroy him.
But Jesus withdrew from them with his disciples and came to the seashore, and a great crowd followed him from Galilee and from Judea,
from Jerusalem and from Idumea, from beyond the Jordan, and from the region of Tyre and Sidon. A great multitude heard how much he was doing, and they came to him.
And he told his disciples to get a boat ready for him because of the crowd, so that they would not crush him.
For he was healing many, so that the crowd kept pressing in on him just to touch him. And as many as had illnesses and touched him were healed.
And when the unclean spirits saw him, they fell down before him, crying out and saying: "You are the Son of God."
And Jesus rebuked them sternly, so that they would not make him known.
And he went up on the mountain and called to him those he wanted; and they came to him.
And he appointed the Twelve, so that they would be with him, and he sent them out to preach,
and so that they would have authority to cast out demons.
And he gave them names: to Simon, Peter;
and James the son of Zebedee and John the brother of James, and he gave them the name Boanerges, which means "Sons of Thunder";
Andrew and Philip, Bartholomew and Matthew, Thomas and James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus and Simon the Cananaean,
and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him.
And they came to a house, and the crowd gathered around him again, so that they could not even eat bread.
And when his own people heard of it, they went out to seize him, for they were saying: "He is out of his mind."
And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying: "Beelzebul is with him, and he casts out demons by the prince of demons."
And he called them to him and spoke to them in parables: "How can the devil cast out the devil?
And if a kingdom is divided against a kingdom, that kingdom cannot stand.
And if a house is divided against a house, that house cannot stand.
And if the devil has risen up against himself and is divided, he cannot stand, but he comes to an end.
And no one can enter a strong man's house and carry off his goods as plunder unless he first ties up the strong man; only then can he plunder his house."
Amen, I say to you that all sins and blasphemies will be forgiven to the sons of men, however much they may blaspheme;
but whoever speaks blasphemy against the Holy Spirit has no forgiveness forever, but is liable to eternal judgment.
For they were saying: "He has an unclean spirit with him."
Then his brothers and his mother came, and they stood outside and sent to him and were calling him out.
And a great crowd was sitting around him; and when they said to him, "Behold, your mother and your brothers are standing outside and are looking for you,"
Jesus answered and said: "Who is my mother, or who are my brothers?"
And he looked around at his disciples sitting around him and said: "Behold, my mother and my brothers!
For whoever does the will of God, this one is my brother and my sister and my mother."
Then again he began to teach by the seashore; and a great crowd gathered to him, so that he went into a boat, and he sat in the boat on the sea; and the whole crowd stood on the land at the seashore.
And he taught them many things in parables, and said to them in his teaching:
"Listen to this: A sower went out to sow.
And as he sowed, some fell on the road; the birds came and ate it.
And other seed fell on rocky ground, where there was not much earth, and it sprang up at once, because there was no depth of earth.
And when the sun rose and scorched it, it withered, because its roots had not spread.
And other seed fell among thorns; and the thorns came up and choked it, and it bore no fruit.
And other seed fell on good ground and gave fruit, coming up and growing, and it brought forth thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold."
And he said: "Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!"
And when he was alone, his disciples asked him: "What is this parable?"
And he said to them: "To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God, but for those outside, everything is spoken in parables,
so that seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest they turn and their sin be forgiven them."
And he said to them: "Do you not know this parable? How then will you understand all the parables?
The one who sows, sows the word.
And these are the ones on the road, where the word is sown: when they hear, the devil comes at once and takes the word away from their hearts.
And these are the ones sown on the rocky ground: when they hear the word, they receive it at once with joy,
but because the root does not spread among them and they are short-lived, when tribulation or persecution comes because of the word, they stumble at once.
And those that were sown among the thorns are the ones who hear the word,
and the cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches enter in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
And these are the ones that were sown on good ground: those who hear the word and receive it and bear fruit, thirtyfold and sixtyfold and a hundredfold.
And he said to them: "Is a lamp brought in to be put under a bushel, or set under a bed? Is it not set on a lampstand?
For there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed, nor is anything kept secret except so that it may come into the open.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!"
And he said to them: "Take heed what you hear. With the measure you measure, it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you who hear.
For whoever has, to him it will be given; and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him."
And he said to them: "The kingdom of God is like this: as when a man sows seed on the ground
and sleeps and rises, night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he does not know how.
For the earth bears fruit by itself: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
And when the fruit is ready, at once he sends in the sickle, because the harvest has come."
And he said: "To what shall we liken the kingdom of God? Or what parable shall we use for it?
It is like a grain of mustard seed which is sown in the ground, for it is the smallest of all the seeds that are on the earth.
And when it is sown, it springs up and becomes greater than all the herbs and puts forth very large branches, so that the birds of the sky are even able to dwell under its shade."
And with many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.
And without a parable he said nothing to them; but to his own disciples he explained everything.
On that day, when evening had come, he said to them: "Let us cross over to the other side."
And they left the crowd, and the disciples took him along, just as he was, in the boat; and other boats too were with him.
And at once there arose a great storm of wind, and it was driving the waves into the boat, so that the boat was even filling up.
And he himself was at the end of the boat, asleep. And they woke him and said to him: "Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?"
And he rose and rebuked the wind and the sea and said: "Be silent, and hold your peace!" And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
And he said to them: "Why are you so fearful? How is it that you have no faith?"
And they were afraid with great fear and said to one another: "Who then is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?"
And they came to the other side of the sea, to the country of the Gadarenes.
And as he came out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit came from the tombs to meet him,
who had his dwelling among the tombs, and no one was able to bind him, not even with chains.
For he had often been bound with chains and fetters, and he would burst them and smash them, and no one could restrain him.
And always, night and day, he would wander about the tombs and the mountains, crying out and cutting himself with stones.
And when he saw Jesus from afar, he came running and bowed down to him,
crying out with a loud voice and saying: What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of God Most High? I adjure you by God, do not torment me.
For Jesus was saying to him: You unclean spirit, come out of that man!
And he asked him: What is your name? And he said to him: Legion is my name, for we are many.
And he begged him earnestly not to send them out of the country.
And there was a great herd of swine there, feeding on the mountainside.
And all the demons begged him, saying: Send us to those swine, so that we may enter into them.

And he commanded them, and the unclean spirits came out of the man and entered the swine, and the herd of swine rushed down the steep bank into the sea, for they were about two thousand, and they were drowned in the sea.
But their herdsmen fled and told it in the city and in the villages. And people came out to see what it was that had happened.
And they came to Jesus and saw the demoniac, the one who had had the legion, sitting there, clothed and in his right mind, and they were afraid.
And those who had seen it told them how it had happened to the demoniac, and about the swine.
And they began to beg him to depart from their borders.
And as Jesus was getting into the boat, the man who had formerly been possessed by demons begged him that he might be with him.
And he did not permit him, but said to him: Go to your home, to your own people, and tell them how much the Lord has done for you and how he has had mercy on you.
And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him; and everyone marveled.
And when Jesus had crossed over again to the other side, a great crowd gathered to him. And he was by the seashore,
and behold, one of the rulers of the synagogue came to him, named Jairus; he saw him and fell at his feet.
And he begged him earnestly, saying: My daughter is dying; come and lay your hands on her, so that she may be saved and live.
And Jesus went with him. And a great crowd followed him and pressed upon him.
And there was a certain woman there who had been afflicted with a flow of blood for twelve years.
And she had suffered much at the hands of many physicians and had spent everything she had, and it had been of no benefit to her; instead, she had grown worse.
And when she heard about Jesus, she came up to him through the crowd from behind and touched his garment,
for she was saying in her heart: "If I touch even just his garment, I shall be saved."
And as soon as she touched it, the fountain of her blood immediately dried up, and she knew in her body that she had been healed of her affliction.
But Jesus immediately perceived in himself that power had gone out from him. He turned to the crowd and said: "Who touched my garment?"
But his disciples said to him: "You see this crowd pressing upon you, and you say, 'Who touched me?'"
And he kept looking around to see the one who had done this.
But the woman was afraid and trembling, knowing what had been done to her. She came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.
And he said to her: "Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace, and be whole and free of your affliction!"
And while he was saying this, people from the synagogue ruler's house came and said to him: "Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher any further?"
But when Jesus heard the words they were saying, he said to the synagogue ruler: "Do not be afraid, only believe!"
And he allowed no one to follow with him except Peter and James and John, the brother of James.
And he came to the house of the synagogue ruler and saw a commotion, weeping, and loud wailing.
And he went in and said to them: "Why are you in such commotion, and why do you weep? The child is not dead but asleep."
And they mocked him. But he put out the whole commotion, took the child's father and mother and his disciples, and went in to where the dead child lay.
And he took the child's hand and said to her: "Talitha kum!" which means, translated: "I say to you, child, arise!"
And immediately the girl arose and began to walk, for she was only twelve years old. And they were utterly overcome with great amazement.
And he strictly charged them that no one should learn of this, and he commanded them to give her something to eat.
And he went out from there and came to his own home town, and his disciples followed him.

And it was the Sabbath, and he began to teach them in their synagogue. And many who heard him were astonished and said: "Where did this man get these things? What is this wisdom that has been given to him, and these great mighty works that are done by his hands?
Is this not the carpenter's son, and the son of Mary, and the brother of James and Joses, Judas and Simon? And are not all his sisters here with us?" And they took offense at him.
But Jesus said to them: "A prophet is not without honor except in his own country, among his own kin, and in his own house."
And he did not do a single mighty work there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
And he marveled at their unbelief. And he went around the surrounding villages and taught them.
And he called the twelve to him and began to send them out two by two, and he gave them authority over unclean spirits.
And he commanded them to take nothing for the road except a staff only: no bags, no bread, no copper money in their belts.
And that they should wear sandals, and not put on two garments.
And he said to them: "Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that place."

"And whoever does not receive you or listen to you, when you go out from there, shake off the dust from your feet as a testimony against them. Amen, I say to you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that city."
And they went out and preached that people should repent.
And they cast out many demons, and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.
And King Herod heard of it, for his name had become known, and he said: "John the Baptist has risen from the dead, and that is why powers are at work in him."
And others said: "He is Elijah," or "He is like one of the prophets of old."
When Herod heard this, he said: "John, whom I beheaded, has risen from the dead."
For this Herod had sent and seized John, bound him and put him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, for he had married her.
For John had been saying to Herod: "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife as your wife."
And Herodias held it against him and wanted to kill him, but she could not.
For Herod feared John, and he knew that he was a righteous and holy man, and he protected him and listened to him, and showed him great honor, and heard him gladly.
And an opportune day came, when Herod, on his birthday, prepared a banquet for his officials and his commanders of thousands and the nobles of Galilee,

and the daughter of Herodias came in and danced; and she pleased Herod and those reclining at table with him. And King Herod said to the girl: "Ask me for whatever you wish, and I will give it to you."
And he swore to her: "Whatever you ask, I will give you, up to half of my kingdom."
And she went out and asked her mother: "What shall I ask for?" And she said to her: "The head of John the Baptist."
And the girl went in at once to the king and said: "I want you to give me right now the head of John the Baptist on a platter."
And King Herod became sorrowful, but because of his oath and those reclining at table with him, he did not want to refuse the girl.
And immediately he sent his swordsman and ordered him to bring his head.
And he went and beheaded him in the prison, and brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl brought it to her mother.
And his disciples heard of it, and they came and wrapped his body and buried it in a tomb.
And the apostles of Jesus came and gathered around him, and told him everything they had done and taught.
And Jesus said to them: "Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little." For many were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat bread.
And they went away by themselves in a boat to a deserted place.
And the people saw them going away, and many understood, and they gathered there on foot from all the cities and came to them.
And Jesus went out and saw a great crowd, and he had compassion on them, because they were like sheep that have no shepherd. And he began to teach them a great deal.
And when much time had passed, his disciples came and said to him: "This place is a wilderness, and the hour is already very late.
Send this crowd away, so that they may go into the surrounding villages and countryside and buy food for themselves, for they have nothing to eat."
But he answered and said to them: "You give them something to eat." And they said to him: "Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give them something to eat?"
And Jesus said to them: "How many loaves do you have? Go and see!" And they looked and said: "Five loaves and two fish."
And he commanded them to make all the people sit down in groups, group by group, on the green grass.
And they sat down in ranks, by hundreds and by fifties.

And he took the five loaves and the two fish, and looked up to heaven, and blessed and broke the loaves, and kept giving them to his disciples to set before the people; and he divided the two fish among them all in the same way.
And they all ate and were satisfied.
And they took up twelve baskets full of the leftover broken pieces, and of the fish as well.
And those who had eaten were about five thousand men.
And immediately he made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side of the sea, to Bethsaida, while he sent the crowd away.
And he took leave of them and went up the mountain to pray.
And when evening came, the boat was out in the middle of the sea, and he himself was alone on the land.
And he saw them struggling as they rowed the boat, for the wind was against them. And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus came to them, walking on the sea, and he meant to pass by them.
But when they saw him walking on the sea, they thought it was some kind of apparition, and they cried out.
For they all saw him and were terrified. And immediately he spoke to them and said: "Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid!"
And he went up into the boat with them, and the wind ceased; and his disciples were utterly astonished.
For they had not understood about the loaves, because their hearts were hardened.
And they crossed over and came to the land of Gennesaret.
And as soon as they came out of the boat, the people of that place immediately recognized him.
And they ran about through all that countryside and began to bring all the sick on beds to wherever they heard he was.

And wherever he went, into villages, cities, or farms, they laid their sick in the marketplaces and begged him that they might touch even just the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched him were healed.
And the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around him.
And they saw some of his disciples eating bread with defiled hands, that is, with unwashed hands, and they found fault,
For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands up to the elbow, for they held to the teaching handed down by the elders.

And when they come in from the marketplaces, they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other things that they have received to keep: the washing of cups and pitchers and cauldrons and couches.
Then those Pharisees and scribes asked him: "Why do your disciples not walk according to the teaching of the elders, but eat bread with unwashed hands?"
But Jesus answered and said to them: "Well did the prophet Isaiah speak about you hypocrites, as it is written: 'This people honours me with their lips, but their hearts are far removed from me.'
'In vain do they serve me, teaching the commandments and teachings of men.'
You have abandoned the commandment of God and you hold to the teaching of men: the washing of cups and pitchers; and you do many other such things."
And he said to them: "Well do you set aside the commandment of God, so that you may establish your own teaching.
For Moses said: 'Honour your father and your mother'; and: 'Whoever speaks evil of father or mother, let him surely die.'
But you say: 'If a man says to his father or mother, "Korban" (that is, a gift), "whatever you might have had as benefit from me" —'
then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father and mother.
And you have made the word of God void by that teaching of yours which you teach; and you do many things like these."
And he called all the people to him and said to them: "Listen to me, all of you, and understand.
There is nothing outside a man that enters into him which can defile him; but what comes out of him, that is what defiles the man.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!"
And when he had gone into the house away from the people, his disciples asked him about the parable.
And he said to them: "Are you also so without understanding? Do you not know that whatever enters a man from outside does not defile him?
For it does not enter the heart but the belly, and it goes out through the drain, purifying all foods."
And he said: "What comes out of a man defiles the man.
For from within, out of the heart of men, come evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, thefts, murders,
covetousness and wickedness, deceit, impurity, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness.
All these evil things come out from within and defile the man."
And from there he arose and went away to the region of Tyre and Sidon. And he entered a house and did not want anyone to know of it, but he could not be hidden.
For a certain woman whose daughter was afflicted by an unclean spirit heard about him, and she came and fell at his feet.
Now the woman was a gentile, by race a Syrophoenician from the seacoast, and she begged him to drive the demon out of her daughter.
But Jesus said to her: "Let the children be filled first, for it is not good to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs."
But she answered and said to him: "Lord, for even the dogs under the table eat of the children's crumbs."
And Jesus said to her: "For that word, go! The demon has gone out of your daughter."
And that woman went away to her house and found that the demon had gone out, and her daughter was clothed, sitting on the bed.
And then again he went out from the borders of Tyre and Sidon and came to the Sea of Galilee, through the midst of the borders of the Decapolis.
And they brought to him a deaf man who spoke with difficulty, and they begged him to lay his hand on him.
And he took him aside from the crowd by himself, and put his fingers into his ears, and spat and touched his tongue,
and he looked up to heaven and sighed and said to him: "Ephphatha!" which is: "Be opened!"
And immediately his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosed, and he spoke rightly.
And he commanded them to tell no one; but the more he commanded them, the more they spread it abroad.
And they were exceedingly amazed and said: "He does all things well: he makes the deaf hear and the mute speak."
In those days, again, there was a great crowd, and they had nothing to eat. He called his disciples and said to them:
"I have compassion on this crowd, for it is three days now that they have been staying with me, and they have nothing to eat.
And if I send them away fasting to their homes, they will faint on the way, for some of them have come from far away."
And his disciples answered and said to him: "From where can we satisfy so great a crowd with bread here in the wilderness?"
And he asked them: "How many loaves do you have?" And they said to him: "Seven."
And he ordered the crowd to sit down on the ground, and he took the seven loaves, gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and they set them before the crowd.
And he also gave a few fish, and he blessed those too and ordered them to be set before them.
And they ate and were satisfied; and they took up the leftover fragments, seven baskets.
And those who had eaten were about four thousand; and he sent them away.
And immediately Jesus got into the boat with his disciples and went to the region of Magdala.
And the Pharisees came out and began to dispute with him, and they asked him for a sign from heaven, testing him.
And he sighed in his spirit and said: "Why does this generation seek a sign? Amen, I say to you: no sign will be given to this generation."
And he left them, and again got into the boat and went away to the other side.
And they had forgotten to take bread, and they had only one loaf with them in the boat.
And Jesus charged them and said to them: "Look, and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of the Herodians."
But they were reasoning with one another and saying, "We have no bread."
And Jesus knew it and said to them, "Why are you reasoning in your hearts, you of little faith, that you have no bread? Do you not yet understand, and do you not remember? Are your hearts blinded?
You have eyes and do not see, and you have ears and do not hear. Do you not understand, and do you not remember?
When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments did you take up?" And they said to him, "Twelve."
"And when I broke the seven for the four thousand, how many hampers of fragments did you take up?" And they said to him, "Seven."
And Jesus said to them, "How is it that you do not understand?"
And he came to Bethsaida, and they brought a blind man to him and begged him to touch him.
And he took his hand and led him outside the village, and he spat on his eyes and laid his hand on him, and asked him whether he saw anything.
And he looked up and said, "I see people like trees walking about."
And then he again laid his hands on his eyes and opened them; and he looked up and was restored, and he saw everything clearly.
And he sent him away to his home and said to him, "Go to your home; and when you enter the village, do not tell anything to anyone in the village."
And Jesus and his disciples went out to the villages of Caesarea Philippi, and on the way he asked his disciples, saying to them, "Who do people say that I am?"
And they answered and said to him, "John the Baptist"; and others, "Elijah"; and others, "One of the prophets."
Jesus said to them, "But who do you say that I am?" Peter answered and said to him, "You are the Christ."
And he sternly charged them not to tell anyone about him.
And he began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, and be killed, and rise again on the third day.
And he spoke this word openly. And Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him for this word.
But he turned around and, seeing his disciples, he rebuked Peter and said to him, "Get behind me, devil, for you are not minding the things of God, but the things of men."
And he called the crowd to him together with his disciples and said to them, "Whoever wishes to come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.
For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; and whoever loses his life for my sake or for the sake of the gospel will save it.
What profit is it to a person if he gains this whole world and forfeits his own soul?
Or what will a person give in exchange for his soul?
For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man also will be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels."
And he said to them, "Amen, I say to you, there are some of those standing here who will not see the taste of death until they see the kingdom of God coming with power."
And after six days Jesus took Peter and James and John and led them up a high mountain by themselves alone, and he was changed into another form before them.
And his clothing became shining and pure white like snow, whiter than any fuller on earth could whiten it.
And Moses appeared to them together with Elijah, and they were with Jesus and were talking.
And Peter answered and said to Jesus: "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three tents here: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
For he did not know what to answer, because they were frightened.
And a cloud came and overshadowed them, and a voice came out of the cloud and said: "This is my beloved Son; listen to him."
And suddenly they looked around and saw no one, but only Jesus with them.
And as they were coming down from the mountain, he ordered them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
And they kept that saying to themselves, and they questioned one another: "What is this 'when he rises from the dead'?"
And they asked him and said to him: "Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"
And he answered and said to them: "Elijah does come and restores all things. And how is it written of the Son of Man that he must suffer much and be treated with contempt?
But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, as it is written of him."
And he came to his disciples and saw a crowd around them, and scribes were arguing with them.
And immediately the whole crowd saw him and were amazed, and they ran up and greeted him.
And he asked the scribes and said: "What are you arguing about with one another?"
And one of the crowd answered him and said: "Teacher, I brought my son to you, who has a mute spirit.
And wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams, and grinds his teeth, and becomes rigid. And I told your disciples to heal him, and they could not."
Jesus answered and said: "O unbelieving generation! How long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him here to me!"
And they brought him to him. And when he saw him, immediately the unclean spirit threw him down; and when he fell on the ground, he rolled about and foamed.
And Jesus asked his father: "How long has it been since this happened to him?" And he said: "From childhood.
And often it has thrown him into fire and into water, to destroy him. But if you can do anything, help us, Lord, and have mercy on us."
And Jesus said to him: "If you can believe, all things are possible to one who believes."
And immediately the father of the child cried out and said with tears: "I believe; help my unbelief."
And when Jesus saw that a crowd was gathering around him, he rebuked the spirit and said to the mute and deaf spirit: "I command you: come out of him and never enter him again!"
And it cried out and convulsed him violently, and came out of him; and he became like a dead man, so that many even said: "He has died."
But Jesus took his hand and raised him up, and he stood up.
And when Jesus went into the house, his disciples asked him privately: "Why could we not drive it out?"
And he said to them: "This kind cannot come out except by prayer and fasting."
And they went out from there and passed through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know.
For he was teaching his disciples and saying to them: "The Son of Man is delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill him; and after he has died, on the third day he will rise."
But they did not understand this saying, and they were afraid to ask him.
And he came to Capernaum. And when he had entered the house, he asked them what they had been arguing about with one another on the way.
But they were silent, for on the way they had been saying to one another: "Which of us is the greatest?"
And he sat down and called the twelve and said to them: "Whoever of you wants to be first, let him be the least of all and the servant of all."
And he brought a child and set him in their midst, and he took him in his arms and said to them:
"Whoever receives one of these children for my name's sake receives me; and whoever receives me receives not me, but the one who sent me."
John answered him and said: "Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name who is not one of us, and we tried to stop him, because he does not follow us."
But he said: "Do not stop him, for there is no one who does a mighty work in my name and is able to speak evil of me."
"For whoever is not against us is on our side."
"Whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in my name because you belong to Christ, amen I tell you, he will not lose his reward."
"And whoever causes one of the little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if a millstone, one turned by a donkey, were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea."
"And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life without a hand than to have two hands and go into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire,"
"where their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched."
"And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire,"
"where their worm never comes to an end, and the fire is not quenched."
"And if your eye leads you astray, pull it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the Gehenna of unquenchable fire,"
"where their worm never comes to an end, and the fire is not quenched."
"For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt."
"Salt is good, but if salt loses its saltiness, what will season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another."
And Jesus got up and left that place and came to the region of Judea beyond the Jordan. The crowds gathered to him again, and he taught them again, as was his custom.
And the Pharisees came to him and asked him: "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?" They were testing him.
But he answered and said to them: "What did Moses command you?"
And they said to him: "Moses ordered that a bill of separation be given and that she be sent away."
Jesus answered and said to them: "Because of your hardness of heart Moses wrote that commandment."
"But from the beginning of creation God made them male and female, and said:"
"'For this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother and be joined to his wife,'"
"'and the two of them shall be one flesh,' so that they are no longer two, but one flesh."
"God has joined them together; let no man separate them."
And afterward, when he was in the house, his disciples again questioned him about this same matter.
And Jesus said to them: "If a husband sends away his wife and marries another, he has committed adultery."
"And if a wife goes away from her husband and is married to another, she too has committed adultery."
And they were bringing children to him, so that he might lay his hand on them; but the disciples were hindering those who were bringing them.
When Jesus saw this, he was angry with them and said: "Let those children come to me and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these."
"Amen, I say to you: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will not enter it."
And he embraced them, laid his hands upon them, and blessed them.

And as he went out onto the road, behold, a certain rich man came running to him and knelt before him, and he entreated him and said: "Good teacher, what deed must I do so that I may inherit eternal life?"
But Jesus said to him: "Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone."
"You know the commandments: do not kill, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not fail to do good, honor your father and your mother."
And he answered and said to him: "All these I have done from my youth; what do I still lack?"

And Jesus looked at him and loved him, and said to him: "If you wish to be perfect, you still lack one thing: go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; take up the cross and come, follow me."
But he was grieved at this word and went away sorrowful, for he had very many possessions.
And Jesus looked around and said to his disciples: "With difficulty will those who have wealth enter the kingdom of God."
And the disciples were amazed at this word, but Jesus answered again and said to them: "How hard it is for those who trust in riches to enter the kingdom of God!"
"It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God."
And they were astonished all the more and said to one another: "Then who can be saved?"
Jesus looked at them and said: "With men it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God."
Peter began to speak to him and said: "Look, we have left everything and followed you."

Jesus answered and said to them: "Amen, I say to you: there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or fields for my sake and for the sake of this gospel
who will not receive a hundredfold now, in this time: houses and brothers and sisters, fathers and mothers and children and fields, after persecution, and in the age to come eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and the last first."

And they were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going ahead of them, and the disciples were amazed. And they followed him and were afraid. And again he took the twelve aside and began to tell them about what was going to happen to him:
"Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn him to death and hand him over to the gentiles,
and they will mock him and torment him and spit on him and kill him, and on the third day he will rise."
And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to him and said: "Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask of you."
And he said to them: "What do you want from me, that I should do for you?"
And they said to him: "Grant us that we may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory."
But Jesus said to them: "You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, and to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?"
And they said to him: "We are able." And Jesus said to them: "The cup that I drink you will indeed drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you will be baptized;
but to sit at my right hand and at my left is not mine to give; rather, it is for those for whom it has been prepared."
And when the ten heard this, they began to be angry with James and John.
But Jesus called them and said to them: "You know that those who are regarded as rulers of the gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
But it shall not be so among you; rather, whoever wishes to be great among you shall be your servant;
and whoever wishes to be first among you shall be the slave of all.
For the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many."
And they came to Jericho. And as Jesus and his disciples were leaving Jericho, and a great crowd with them, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind man, was sitting beside the road begging.
And when he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out and say: "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
And many rebuked him, telling him to be silent; but he cried out all the more: "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Jesus stopped and ordered him to be called. And they called the blind man and said to him: "Do not be afraid; get up, he is calling you."
And he threw off his garment, got up, and came to him.
Jesus answered and said to him: "What do you want me to do for you?" And the blind man said to him: "Rabbi, that I may receive my sight."
And Jesus said to him: "[?] go; your faith has saved you." And immediately he received his sight and followed him on the road.
And when they drew near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, he sent two of the disciples
and said to them: "Go into that village which is before you; and as you enter it, you will find a colt tied, on which no one has yet sat; untie it and bring it to me.
And if anyone says anything to you, tell him: 'The Lord needs it,' and he will send it here at once."
And they went and found the colt tied at the door, outside at the entrances, and they untied it.
And some of those standing there said to them: "What are you doing, untying that colt?"
And they told them just as Jesus had commanded them; and they let them go.
And they brought the colt to Jesus and threw their garments on it, and he sat on it.
And many spread their garments on the road, and others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
And those who went ahead and those who followed behind cried out and said: "Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the coming of King David, our father! Save us, you who are in the highest!"
And Jesus entered Jerusalem and the temple and looked around at everything, for it was already the hour of evening. And he went out to Bethany with the twelve.
And on the next day, as they came out from Bethany, he was hungry.
And he saw from afar a fig tree that had leaves, and he went to see whether he might find anything on it. And when he came to it, he found nothing but leaves only, for it was not the season for figs.
And he said to it: "May no one ever eat fruit from you again, forever." And his disciples heard this.

And they came to Jerusalem, and Jesus entered the temple and began to drive out the sellers and the buyers from the temple; and he overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of the dove-sellers.
And he would not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple.
And he taught and said: "It is written: 'My house shall be called a house of prayer by all the nations,' but you have made it a den of robbers."
And the chief priests and the scribes heard this and sought how they might destroy him; and they were afraid of him, for all the people were astonished at his teaching.
And when it was evening, they went out of the city.
And as they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.
And Peter remembered and said to him: "Rabbi, look, the fig tree which you cursed has withered."
Jesus answered and said to them:

"Have faith in God! Amen, I say to you: whoever says to this mountain, 'Be uprooted and fall into the sea!' and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says will happen, it will be so for him.
Therefore I say to you: whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you will receive it, and it will be yours.
And when you stand in prayer, forgive, if you have anything evil against anyone, so that your Father also, who is in heaven, may forgive you your sins."
And they came again to Jerusalem. And as he was walking about in the temple, the chief priests and the scribes and the elders came to him
and said to him: By what authority are you doing this, and who gave you this authority to do this?
But Jesus answered and said to them: I too will ask you one question, and you answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do this:
Was the baptism of John from heaven, or from men? Tell me.
But they reasoned among themselves and said: If we say, 'It was from heaven,' he will say to us, 'Why then did you not believe him?'
And if we say, 'From men,' we are afraid of the people, for all knew of John that he was truly a prophet.
And they answered and said to Jesus: We do not know. — And Jesus answered and said to them: Neither will I tell you by what authority I do this.
And he began to speak to them in parables: A certain man planted a vineyard, and put a wall around it, and made a winepress, and built a tower, and gave it to tenant farmers and went away.
And at the time of the fruit he sent a servant to those tenants, to receive the fruit of the vineyard.
But they seized him and beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
Then again he sent another servant, and him too they set upon again, beat him, and sent him away insulted.
And again he sent another, and him too they killed; and many others — some they tormented and some they killed.
Last of all, he had one son, his beloved, and he sent him to them, for he said: 'They will respect my son.'
But those tenants said to one another: This is his heir; come, let us kill him, and this inheritance will be ours.
And they seized him and killed him and threw him out of the vineyard.
9. Now what will the lord of the vineyard do to them? He will come and destroy those tenants and give the vineyard to others.
Have you not even read this scripture: 'The stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner'?
this was from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes'?"
And they sought to seize him, and they were afraid of the people, for they knew that he had spoken the parable about them. And they left him and went away.
And they sent to him some of the Pharisees and the Herodians, to catch him in his words.

And they came and asked him: Teacher, we know that you are truthful and have no concern for anyone, for you do not look at the face of men, but truly teach the way of God. Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar or not? Shall we give, or shall we not give?
15. But he knew their hypocrisy and said to them: Why do you test me? Bring me a denarius, that I may see it.
And they brought it. And he said to them: Whose is this image and inscription? And they said to him: Caesar's.
Jesus answered and said to them: Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's. And they marveled at this and went away.
And Sadducees came to him, who say that there is no resurrection, and they asked him, saying:
19. Teacher, Moses wrote thus for us: if anyone's brother dies and has a wife, and leaves no child, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers among us. And the first took a wife and died, and no child was left.
21. And the second took her and died, and no child was left, and the third likewise,
…up to the seventh, and none left a child. Last of all the woman died.
Now then, in the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be of them? For all seven had her as wife.
Jesus answered and said to them: Is it not for this reason that you go astray, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God?
For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but they are like the angels in heaven.
And as for the dead rising, have you not read in the book of Moses, at the bush, how God spoke to him and said: I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?
He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living. You are greatly mistaken.
And one of the scribes came to him. When he heard them, how they were disputing with him, he knew that he had answered them well, and he too asked him: Which is the first commandment of all?
And Jesus said to him: The first of all the commandments is this: Hear, O Israel, the Lord your God, the Lord is one;
and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength. This is the first commandment.
And the second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. There is no other commandment greater than these.
The scribe said to him: Well said, Teacher; you have spoken truly, that God is one, and there is no other besides him;

and to love him with all the heart, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and with all the understanding, and to love one's neighbor as oneself — this is greater than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.
And Jesus saw that he had answered wisely, and said to him: You are not far from the kingdom of God. And no one dared to question him any more.
Jesus answered and said to them, as he was teaching in the temple: How then do the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
For David himself says by the Holy Spirit: The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, until I put your enemies beneath your feet.
David himself calls him Lord; so how is he his son? And the great crowd listened to him gladly.
And he said to them in his teaching: Beware of the scribes, who like to walk about in fine robes and to be greeted in the marketplaces,
and to have the high seats in the synagogue and the first places at banquets;
who devour the houses of widows and for a pretense pray at length. They will receive greater condemnation.
And Jesus sat down opposite the treasury and watched how the people put copper coins into the treasury. And many rich people put in a great deal.
And a poor widow came and put in two small coins, which is a quadrans.
And Jesus called his disciples to him and said to them: Amen, I say to you, this poor widow has put more into this treasury than all the others.
For they all put in out of their abundance, but she, out of her want, put in everything she had, her whole living.
And as he was going out of the temple, one of his disciples said to him: Teacher, look, what stones and what buildings!
Jesus answered and said to him: Do you see these great buildings? There will not be left a stone upon a stone that will not be thrown down.
And as he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately:
"Tell us, when will this be, and what will be the signs when all these things are about to be fulfilled?"
Jesus answered and said to them: "Take care that no one leads you astray.
For many will come in my name and say, 'I am he,' and they will lead many astray.
When you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be alarmed, for this must happen, but it is not yet the end.

For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be earthquakes in various places, and there will be famines and disturbances. All this is the beginning of the birth pains.

But take care for yourselves, for they will hand you over to councils, and in synagogues they will torment you, and you will stand before kings and rulers for my sake, as a testimony to them and to all the nations.
But first this gospel must be preached.

And when they bring you to hand you over, do not worry beforehand, nor rehearse what you will say, but whatever is given to you in that hour, say that, for it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
And brother will hand over brother to death, and father his child, and children will rise up against their parents and put them to death.
And you will be hated by all because of my name; but whoever endures to the end will be saved.

But when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not to be — let the one who reads understand — then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.
And let the one who is on the roof not come down into the house, nor go in to take anything from his house.
And let the one who is out in the field not turn back to take his garment.
But woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!
But pray that your flight may not be in winter.
For those days will be days of affliction such as has never been from the beginning of what God created until now, and never will be.
And if God had not shortened those days, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the elect, whom he has chosen, he has shortened those days.
Then if anyone says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ,' or 'There,' do not believe it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise and will perform signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if they could, even the elect.
But you, see and take care; behold, I have told you everything beforehand.
But in those days, after that affliction, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light;
and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds with great power and glory.
And then he will send out his angels and gather his elect from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.
Now learn this parable from the fig tree: when its branches become tender and the leaves come out, you know that summer is near.
So also you, when you see all these things come to pass, know that it is near, at the doors.
Amen, I say to you: this generation will not pass away until all these things take place.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.
But concerning that day and hour no one knows, neither the angels in heaven nor the Son, but only the Father.
But take heed, be watchful and pray, for you do not know when that time will be.
It is like a man going on a journey, who leaves his house and gives authority to his servants, and to each one his work, and commands the doorkeeper to be watchful.
Watch therefore, for you do not know when the lord of the house will come: in the evening, or at midnight, or at cockcrow, or at dawn.
Lest he come suddenly and find you sleeping.
And what I say to you, I say to all: be watchful.
Now the Passover, that is, the Passion, and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were two days away. And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might seize Jesus by deceit and kill him.
But they said: "Not during this feast, lest there be an uproar among the people."

And while Jesus was at Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, and was reclining at table, a woman came who had an alabaster flask of ointment of pure nard, very costly; and she broke the alabaster flask and poured it on his head.

There were some who were murmuring among themselves and saying: "Why was this ointment wasted? For it could have been sold for more than three hundred drachmas and given to the poor." And they were angry with her.
But Jesus said to them: "Let her alone; why do you trouble her? For she has done a good deed to me.
For the poor are always with you, and whenever you wish, you can do good to them; but I am not always with you.
She has done what she could; she has anointed my body with ointment beforehand for my burial.
Amen, I say to you: wherever this gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her."
And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests in order to hand him over to them.
And when they heard this from him, they rejoiced and promised to give him silver. And he sought how he might hand him over to them at a convenient time.
And on the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they sacrificed the Passover lamb, his disciples said to Jesus: "Where do you wish us to go and prepare for you, so that you may eat this Passover?"
And he sent two of his disciples and said to them: "Go into the city, and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you; follow him wherever he goes in.
And say to the master of the house: 'The Teacher says: Where is the lodging where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?'
And he will show you a large upper room, furnished and prepared; there make ready for us."
And his disciples went out and came into the city and found it just as Jesus had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
And when it was evening, he came with the Twelve.
And as they were reclining at table and eating, Jesus said to them: "Amen, I say to you that one of you will betray me, one who is eating with me."
And they began to be sorrowful and to say to him, one by one: "Surely it is not I?" And another said: "Surely it is not I?"
And Jesus answered and said to them: "One of the Twelve, the one who dips his hand into this dish with me, he will betray me."
The Son of Man indeed goes, as it is written of him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed; it would have been better for him if that man had not been born."
And while they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, gave it to them, and said: "Take and eat, for this is my body."
And he took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
And he said to them: "This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many."
But amen, I say to you that I will no longer drink of this fruit of this vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God."
And after they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
And Jesus said to them: "You will all fall away because of me this night, for it is written: 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of his flock will be scattered.'
But after my resurrection I will go before you to Galilee."
But Peter said to him: "Even if all fall away, yet I will never fall away."
Jesus said to him: "Amen, I say to you that today, this night, before the cock crows twice, you will deny me three times."
But Peter spoke all the more insistently: "Even if I must die with you, I will never deny you." And all the others said the same thing likewise.
And they came to a village whose name was Gethsemane. And Jesus said to his disciples: "Sit here while I pray."
And he took Peter and James and John with him, and he began to be distressed and troubled.
And he said to them: "My soul is sorrowful even unto death; stay here and keep watch."
And he went a little farther, fell on the ground, and prayed that, if it were possible, that hour might pass from him.
And he said: "Abba, Father, all things are possible for you; let this cup pass from me. Yet not what I will, but what you will."
And he came and found them sleeping, and he said to Peter: "Simon, are you asleep? Could you not keep watch with me for one hour?
Keep watch and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit is eager, but the flesh is weak."
And again he went away and prayed, and said the same words.
And he returned again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy, and they did not know what to answer him.
And he came a third time and said to them: "Sleep on now and take your rest. The end has arrived, and the hour has come. Behold, lo, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
Get up, and let us go from here. Look, the one who betrays me has come near.
And immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas Iscariot came, one of the Twelve, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
Now the one who betrayed him had given them a sign and said to them: "The one I kiss is the man. Seize him and lead him away carefully."
And immediately he came and went up to him and said: "Rabbi! Rabbi!" And he kissed him.
Then they laid their hands on him and seized him.
And one of those standing by drew a sword and struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
Jesus answered and said to them: "You have come out with swords and clubs to seize me as if against a robber.
Day after day I was with you in the temple, teaching, and you did not seize me. But this is so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled."
Then all his disciples left him and fled.
And a certain young man was following him, wearing a linen cloth over his naked body. And the other young men seized him.
And he left the linen cloth behind and fled from them naked.
And they led Jesus to Caiaphas the high priest. And all the chief priests and the scribes and the elders gathered together.
But Peter followed him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest, and he sat with the servants and warmed himself before the light of the fire.
Now the chief priests and the whole council were looking for witnesses against Jesus in order to put him to death, and they did not find any.
For many gave false testimony against him, and their testimonies did not agree.
And some others stood up and gave false testimony against him, saying,
"We heard him say: 'I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and on the third day I will build another, not made with hands.'"
And even so their testimonies did not agree.
And the high priest stood up in their midst and questioned Jesus, saying: "Do you answer nothing to what these men testify against you?"
But Jesus was silent and answered them nothing. And again the high priest questioned him a second time and said to him: "Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?"
And Jesus answered him: "I am. And from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Powers and coming with the clouds of heaven."
Then the high priest tore his garment and said: "Why do we need witnesses?
You have all heard the blasphemy from him. What is your will?" Then they all condemned him as deserving death.

And some began to spit on him, to cover his face, and to strike him with their fists, and they said to him: "Prophesy to us, Christ: who is it that struck you?" And the servants took him to be slapped.
And while Peter was in the courtyard, one of the high priest's maidservants came.
And when she saw him warming himself, she looked at him and said to him: "You too were with Jesus of Nazareth."
But he denied it and said: "I do not know, nor do I understand what you are saying." And Peter went out into the outer courtyard, and the cock crowed.
And the maidservant saw him again and began to say to those standing by: "This man too is one of them."
But he denied it again. And after a little while those standing by said to Peter: "Truly you are one of them, for you are a Galilean, and your speech also gives you away."
But Peter began to curse and to swear: "I do not know this man of whom you speak."
And immediately the cock crowed a second time. And Peter remembered the word that Jesus had said to him: "Before the cock crows twice, you will deny me three times." And he began to weep.
And immediately, at dawn, the chief priests took counsel with the elders and the scribes and the whole council. And they bound Jesus and led him away and handed him over to Pilate.
And Pilate questioned him and said to him: "Are you the King of the Jews?" And Jesus answered and said to him: "You say so."
And the chief priests accused him of many things.
And Pilate questioned him again and said to him: "Do you answer nothing? See how many things they testify against you!"
But Jesus answered nothing more, so that Pilate was amazed.
And at each feast he used to release to them one prisoner, whomever they asked for.
And there was a certain Barabbas, bound with the rioters who had committed murder in the riot.
And the crowd cried out, asking him to do as he always granted them.
And Pilate answered and said to them: "Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?"
For he knew that the chief priests had handed him over out of envy.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd, so that he would release Barabbas to them instead.
And Pilate answered again and said to them: "What then do you want me to do with the one whom you call the King of the Jews?"
And they cried out again and said to him: "Crucify him!"
And Pilate said to them: "What evil has he done?" But they cried out all the more and said: "Crucify him!"
And Pilate, wishing to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas to them; and he had Jesus flogged with a whip and handed him over to them to be crucified.
And the soldiers led him into the inner courtyard, which is the praetorium, and they called together the whole company [lit. "kindred"].
And they clothed him in purple and put on him a crown woven of thorns.
And they began to salute him and said: "Hail, King of the Jews!"
And they struck him on the head with a reed and spat on him, and they knelt down and bowed down to him.
And when they had mocked him, they stripped him of the purple robe, put his own clothes back on him, and led him out to crucify him.
And they forced a passer-by, a certain Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross.
And they brought him to Golgotha, the place whose name translated means the Place of the Skull.
And they offered him wine mixed with myrrh to drink, but he did not take it.
And they crucified him and divided his clothes, casting lots over them to decide who would take what.
It was the third hour when they crucified him.
And the inscription of the charge against him was written thus: This is the King of the Jews.
And with him they crucified two robbers, one on his right and one on his left.
And the scripture was fulfilled which says: He was counted among the lawless.
And those passing by reviled him, shaking their heads and saying: Aha, you who would destroy this temple and build it again on the third day,
save yourself and come down from the cross.
In the same way the chief priests, together with the scribes, mocked him and said: He saved others; he cannot save himself, the Christ, the King of Israel!
Let him come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe. And those who were crucified with him also reproached him in the same way.
And when it was the sixth hour, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.
And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice and said: Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which translated means: God, my God, why have you forsaken me?
And some of those standing by heard it and said: Look, he is calling Elijah.
And one ran and filled a sponge with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave him to drink, saying: Leave him; let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down.
But Jesus cried out with a loud voice and gave up his spirit.
And the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
And when the centurion who stood before him saw that he cried out thus and gave up his spirit, he said: Truly this man was the Son of God.
There were also women watching from a distance, among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the Less and of Joses, and Salome,
who, when he was in Galilee, had followed him and served him; and many other women who had come up with him to Jerusalem.
And as evening was coming on — for it was the Day of Preparation, that is, the day before the Sabbath —
Joseph of Arimathea came, an honourable councillor, who was himself also waiting for the kingdom of God; he took courage and went in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
But Pilate was amazed that he was already dead, and he summoned the centurion and asked him whether he had died so soon.
And he learned this from the centurion, and he granted the body to Joseph.
And Joseph bought linen, took him down from the cross, wrapped him in the linen, and laid him in a tomb that had been hewn out of the rock. Then he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses were there, and they saw where he was being laid.
And when the sabbath had passed, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so that they might come and anoint him.
And very early in the morning on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb, just as the sun was rising.
And they were saying to one another: "Who will roll the stone away from the door of the tomb for us?"
And they looked up and saw that the stone had been rolled away, and it was very large.
And when they went into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, dressed in a white garment, and they were alarmed.
But he said to them: "Do not be alarmed! You are looking for Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He has risen; he is not here. Look, here is the place where they laid him.
But go and tell his disciples and Peter: 'Look, he is going ahead of you to Galilee. There you will see him, just as he told you.'"
And when they heard this, they went out and fled from the tomb, for they were trembling and astonished. And they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.
Now when he had risen early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out.
She went and told those who had been with him, who were mourning and weeping.
And when they heard that he was alive and had appeared to her, they did not believe it.
After this he appeared in another form to two of them as they were walking along, on their way to a village.
And they came and told the others, and the others did not believe them either.
Last of all he appeared to the eleven as they were sitting at table. He rebuked them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they had not believed those who had seen him risen.
And he said to them: "Go into all the world and preach this gospel to all creation.
Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, and whoever does not believe will be condemned.
And these signs will follow those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak in new tongues;
they will take hold of serpents; and if they drink anything deadly, it will not harm them at all; they will lay their hands on the sick, and the sick will recover."
Then the Lord, after these words to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
And they went out and preached throughout the whole earth. The Lord helped them and confirmed this word through the signs that followed it.
